summary: A skinned MeshInstance3D with a named-bind Skin, skeleton=^"..", added as a child of the existing code-built Skeleton3D, follows HumanoidRig.advance() with zero latency and needs no change to the animation path. Hurtboxes, rig points, followers, the hit-flash anchors, set_shown and the KO blink-off are all mesh-independent and keep working. There is one real gap: during a ragdoll the skin shows the simulator's raw output, not Ragdoll._visual (which blends head and arms at 0.45 and eases launches). A write-back of _visual into the skeleton inside Ragdoll._process_modification_with_delta fixes it (gap goes from up to 0.115 m to 0.0000 in the probe). The hit flash works on skinned meshes unchanged. VERTEX in a spatial vertex() is the skinned position, so DamageLook's object-space triplanar and any object-space halftone will swim on a skinned body. A single next_pass slot per material collides with an outline-as-next_pass. The big cost is on the test side. tests/fp_view.gd ray-casts only Box, Cylinder, Capsule and Sphere meshes by part name, and about 14 test files plus the M3 readability probe depend on it. PlayerCharacter._configure_rig is also used by tests to dress scratch rigs, so the player's skinned art must not hang there. The rest skeleton, with a full joint table at 1.8 m, has identity rotations and arms straight down. A skinned mesh scales to other heights through its Skin binds. Imported A-pose or T-pose meshes need binds carrying the pose, or a Blender re-pose to arms-down. Everything was run as scratch scripts with no tracked file touched.
key_facts: HumanoidRig.build() order (humanoid_rig.gd:187): skeleton -> materials -> _warm_flash -> meshes -> points -> hurtboxes -> animation -> start idle -> advance(0). All config (height, stance, wrapped_hands, first_person_body, colours, actor) is set before build() by CombatActor._ensure_body (combat_actor.gd:1561) via the virtual _configure_rig; enemy/player scenes contain no Rig node.

Every body part is a primitive MeshInstance3D parented to a plain Node3D follower 'Bone<Name>' under the Skeleton3D; followers are set to FK in _refresh_pose (humanoid_rig.gd:1008) or to the ragdoll pose in show_visual_pose (:692). Hurtboxes, rig points (Marker3D children of followers), get_attachment, the weapon, health bars and flash anchors read bones/points only, never meshes.

Counts: 23 bones; 41 primitive meshes for enemies, 45 for the player (wrapped hands), 15 of them FP-hidden; 46 named animation ids, 26 move ids plus 15 enemy move ids (Punk: punk_jab, punk_cross, punk_shove); each clip is 22 rotation tracks plus one Hips position track, rotation-only, so there is no bone stretch.

VERIFIED: a named-bind Skin skinned mesh under the existing skeleton gives render-server skin matrices equal to pose_global * bind, with a gap of 0.0000 against rig FK over idle, jab and flinch, windowed on Metal. It also runs headless with a running ragdoll without errors.

VERIFIED gap: in a partial ragdoll the skin differs from Ragdoll._visual by up to about 0.04 m at the head origin and 0.115 m at the worst bone, because Ragdoll writes only _visual and never set_bone_pose_*. A post-Ragdoll modifier writing _visual's local rotations into the skeleton brings the gap to 0.0000. Put it in ragdoll.gd:614-647.

VERIFIED: hit_flash.gdshader as next_pass on a skinned surface draws the radial white blob correctly. VERIFIED: VERTEX in vertex() is the skinned rig-space position, so object-space triplanar (DamageLook uv1_triplanar) swims on a skinned mesh. Use UVs, vertex colour or a bind-pose position in CUSTOM0 instead. Damage look applies to enemies only (VfxDirector checks the enemy group).

Material coupling: _materials is Dictionary[int, StandardMaterial3D] (one per Paint BODY/PANTS/ACCENT/SKIN/DARK per rig). set_flash uses emission, the contact flash uses mat.next_pass (a single slot, which would collide with an outline pass), and DamageLook.prepare/apply are typed StandardMaterial3D with detail_*/uv1_triplanar. tests test_vfx, test_hit_flash and test_humanoid_rig read rig.get(&'_materials') with that exact type, so keep a separate toon-material dictionary for the skinned path.

FP-hidden layer (render layer 2) is per MeshInstance3D, so the art must be split at authoring time into an FP-hidden mesh and a visible one. Hidden: Chest, UpperChest, Neck, Head, both Shoulders, and the shoulder-end capsules of the upper arms; the elbow-end capsule stays visible. The first-person camera has near 0.05, 90 degrees horizontal FOV, and a lens 0.2 m below EyePoint, about y 1.456 at the throat. Tests judge the elbow end as a rounded cap, so the visible cut needs a closed end. FirstPersonCamera._head_clear_of (:384) reads head-layer mesh AABBs and must move to bones (bind-pose AABB is wrong for skinned meshes).

Rest skeleton at 1.8 m: Hips y 0.975, Spine 1.075, Chest 1.205, UpperChest 1.335, Neck 1.485, Head 1.575; shoulders (+/-0.05, 1.435), upper arms (+/-0.22, 1.425), elbows (+/-0.22, 1.135), wrists (+/-0.22, 0.865); hip joints (+/-0.11, 0.925), knees y 0.505, ankles y 0.085, toes (+/-0.11, 0.035, -0.13). All rotations identity, character faces -Z. Heights scale uniformly by height/1.8 (Bruiser 1.1389, Boss 1.2778).

Height scaling of a skinned mesh authored at 1.8 m is done by Skin binds Transform3D(Basis.IDENTITY*s, -s*rest_global_unscaled.origin); verified at 2.3 m. Bind index order must equal bone index order, so remap ARRAY_BONES by name on load. Never reuse glTF inverse-bind matrices, because exporter bone roll breaks identity-axes bones. Rebuild the Skin from our own rest or arm-down frames.

A-pose or T-pose meshes: either re-pose to arms-down in Blender and apply as rest with the weights kept (then translation-only binds), or carry the swing-only rotation R_i in bind_i = (R_i, joint_in_authoring_pose)^-1. Joint centres must coincide with the table, since hurtboxes, ragdoll anchors and rig points are table-derived. The sole plane must be at y=0 (heel z +0.085, ball z -0.13, toe tip z -0.25, x +/-0.11), or planting sinks or floats the feet. The mesh must face -Z, and an exported glTF needs a 180-degree Y turn.

Tests (read only, not run): tests/fp_view.gd ray_hit supports only Box/Cylinder/Capsule/Sphere, so skinned ArrayMesh parts are invisible to hits(), and mesh_distance null-casts on an ArrayMesh. Real-player-rig tests that need edits: test_grab_view, test_ko_view, test_player_grabbed, test_launch_from_hold, test_health_bars:197 and 94, test_hit_flash and test_vfx material tests, and the M3 readability probe used by test_m3_done_when and test_slice_crowd (R4/R8 would silently under-count skinned Punks). test_humanoid_rig._player_rig (35 uses), enemy_move_checks.fp_telegraph_problems and test_enemy_moves_thug call PlayerCharacter._configure_rig, so do not put the player's art in it.

Ragdoll reads no meshes or followers: it reads rig.animation_pose, skeleton.get_bone_pose inside the modifier and rig_scale, and writes only _visual plus show_visual_pose. The player never ragdolls unless Tuning.ragdoll_player (default false), so the ragdoll write-back affects enemy art only. skeleton.get_bone_pose reads back the animation pose after the update, so nothing outside a modifier can read the pose the skin shows during a ragdoll.

Pitfalls for scratch scripts: godot --headless -s cannot compile scripts that use autoloads at load time, so load() game scripts inside _initialize. Pass --quit-after, or a script that errors before quit() hangs. pkill and kill were denied by the permission classifier, and a stray process can only be stopped through TaskStop.
verified_by_running: Rest skeleton, rig points, hurtboxes and per-part AABBs dumped from a live HumanoidRig at 1.8, 2.05 and 2.3 m (joints.gd, headless); rig_scale is 1.0, 1.1389 and 1.2778, 23 bones, 41 meshes.

Animation, part and ragdoll-body counts, rest-pose part extents and the boxer/relaxed stance joint positions (counts.gd, headless): ANIM_IDS 46, MOVE_IDS 26, enemy move ids 15, 22 rotation tracks plus 1 position track per clip, 41/45 parts, 18 ragdoll bodies, 4 hurt specs, 15 player parts on FP_HIDDEN.

A named-bind Skin skinned procedural mesh under the rig's own Skeleton3D, windowed on Metal: RS skin matrix equals pose*bind (gap 0.0000 vs FK) over idle, jab and flinch. It also renders (screenshots tiles.png and shot2_*.png) and runs headless with a ragdoll without errors.

A partial ragdoll compared the skin against Ragdoll._visual: gap up to 0.115 m worst bone (head about 0.04 m). A post-Ragdoll write-back SkeletonModifier3D reduced it to 0.0000, in headless and windowed runs (ragdoll_vs_skin.gd, skin_exp*.gd, sync_mod.gd). skeleton.get_bone_global_pose reads back the animation pose after the update (headless).

Scale-carrying Skin binds at 2.3 m, Transform3D(Basis.IDENTITY*s, -s*r_unscaled): the skin matrix basis scale is 1.2778 and the unscaled rest joints land exactly on the animated joints (scale_exp.gd).
VERTEX in a spatial vertex() is the skinned position: stripes keyed on v.y stayed horizontal in rig space after a 90 degree head rotation (vertex_exp.gd, vtx_tiles.png).
hit_flash.gdshader as next_pass on a skinned magenta mesh drew the radial flash correctly at the chest (flash_exp.gd, flash_tiles.png).

The Godot class reference (godot-doc) was checked for Skeleton3D.create_skin_from_rest_transforms, MeshInstance3D.skin/skeleton/get_skin_reference, GeometryInstance3D.material_overlay, Material.next_pass and Skin.add_named_bind; the member names exist, but the dump has no descriptions, so behaviour was not confirmed from it.
open_questions: Does the Punk's art hook go in StreetPunk._configure_rig (confirmed hook) and the player's in a separate hook (not _configure_rig)? And is the primitive path kept as the default (Assumption A), or removed for everyone (B, which breaks about 80 primitive-dependent tests)?

FPView strategy for skinned meshes: region proxy primitives, CPU skinning with bone-region bounding volumes, or bone-based comparisons? This is the largest test cost and also affects the M3 readability probe R4 and R8 under Punk art.

Does the player's art cover only arms, legs and shoes with primitive torso and head kept (hybrid), or the whole body? An FP-hidden / visible split with a closed rounded cap mid-upper-arm is needed either way.
Outline and flash pass chaining: next_pass chain versus GeometryInstance3D.material_overlay (not tried).
Damage look on a skinned Punk: damage-mask UVs, vertex colour, or CUSTOM0 bind-pose triplanar?

Which authoring route for the Tripo mesh: Blender re-pose to arms-down with weights kept (translation-only binds), or an A/T-pose mesh with pose-carrying binds. The glTF import details were not tested with a real asset: bind names and indices, the +Z-front export turn, the need for custom_aabb under a flying ragdoll, 8-weight need, skinning cost for six Punks on the M1, and normals under non-unit-scale binds for the 2.05 and 2.3 m bodies.
The deliverable is about 52 KB, over the requested 15-40 KB, because of the test inventory and tables. Trim if the planner wants a shorter map.

summary: Mapped the presentation and tooling that M4's look work touches: game/fx (VfxDirector, ComicSprite, SpeedLines, ImpactFrame, DamageLook, hit_flash.gdshader, VfxArt), tools/gen_fx.gd and its assets, the code-drawn HUD and rear warning, both rooms' rendering setup (RoomKit for the crowd room, a duplicated copy in the frozen test_room.gd), project.godot rendering settings, the tests and bots that pin visuals, and the capture tooling. Key findings: every material in the game is built in GDScript (no scene or .tres holds one), so the toon look hooks in through a few factory functions (HumanoidRig._build_materials, RoomKit.flat_material/grid_material, test_room._flat_material, the two build_environment functions). A depth+normal screen-space edge pass (a full-screen spatial quad) was prototyped in the crowd room and works with MSAA 4x in first person and side view; on the M1 its cost is mostly the depth/normal-roughness buffer request (+2.3 to +3.6 ms), not the taps. M2's VFX set already covers every SPEC §10 item (10 words, 3 bursts, speed lines, droplets, splats, rear-warning burst), and tools/gen_fx.gd regenerates all 29 SVG/PNG pairs byte-identically. No existing act records a Punk 1 m from the lens standing still and in motion; a scratch crowd-room bot proved the recipe, and showed AI-driven motion at 1 m does not work (the Punk attacks then sits in RECOVER). The perf act re-run today was contaminated by machine load; M3's recorded p95 12.2-13.1 ms and spawn hitch 25-31.5 ms are the reference.
key_facts: Materials: all code-built. Characters = 5 StandardMaterial3D per rig (one per PlaceholderBody.Paint) in humanoid_rig.gd:723 _build_materials, field _materials: Dictionary[int, StandardMaterial3D] (line 147); environment = RoomKit.flat_material (room_kit.gd:116) and grid_material (124, grid.gdshader ShaderMaterial); training room has duplicates (test_room.gd:201 and :95); pipe weapon.gd:42; no scene/.tres holds a material.

The two rooms duplicate sky/sun/fog/materials: RoomKit.build_environment (room_kit.gd:49) vs TestRoom._build_environment (test_room.gd:65). Every bot except crowd_bot (combo, vfx, punk, ragdoll, warning) renders in the training room, so the look must land in both. Settings: sky procedural, ambient sky 0.7, FILMIC tonemap, fog 0.008, one DirectionalLight3D (-52,32,0), energy 1.2, shadows to 40 m, no Compositor/CameraAttributes/LUT/glow. project.godot: forward_plus, msaa_3d=2 (4x), 1920x1080 base with 1600x900 window override.

Edge-pass prototype [V]: a QuadMesh(2,2) child of the room with extra_cull_margin 16384 and a spatial shader (unshaded, depth_test_disabled, skip_vertex_transform, POSITION=vec4(VERTEX.xy,1,1)) reading hint_depth_texture and hint_normal_roughness_texture drew clean ink lines in first person and side view with MSAA 4x; HUD unaffected; lines are not MSAA-smoothed (stair-steps). Shader built-ins (INV_PROJECTION_MATRIX) cannot be used inside helper functions, pass them as arguments.

Edge-pass cost on M1 at 1600x900, vsync off, MSAA 4x: base ~10.8-11.3 ms; depth texture 1 tap +2.8; normal-roughness 1 tap +3.6; depth+normal 5 taps ~+4.8; so the cost is requesting the buffers, not the taps. MSAA 4x itself ~2 ms. viewport_get_measured_render_time_gpu returns 0.00 on this Metal setup, so use unvsynced wall time; with vsync on everything reads 16.66.

Hit flash and damage look are bound to StandardMaterial3D: humanoid_rig.gd:521 sets mat.next_pass = flash overlay (tests assert it is the overlay or null: test_hit_flash.gd:154/297/374), set_flash writes emission, DamageLook.prepare/apply (damage_look.gd:61/75) write detail_albedo/uv1_triplanar, test_vfx.gd:688-835 pins the shader-variant stability. A toon ShaderMaterial must re-implement all three; an inverted-hull outline via next_pass conflicts with the flash, so use separate hull meshes (copy layers for FP-hidden parts) or chain.

tests/fp_view.gd raycasts only Box/Cylinder/Capsule/Sphere meshes; 17 test/bot files use it (incl. readability_probe R4/R8). A skinned Punk mesh makes those see nothing until FPView handles ArrayMesh.

VFX set vs SPEC §10: complete (10 words POW BAM SMAK WHAM THUD BOFF KRAK CRUNCH WHUMP KAPOW; burst_small/medium/large; speed_lines sheet of 4 streaks; blood_drop, spit, 3 splats, spray; rear_warning), plus tooth, block/parry/guard-break sparks, 4 damage tiles. tools/gen_fx.gd (679 lines) is seeded and reproduces all 29 SVG + 29 PNG byte-identically [V]; rasterizes with Image.load_svg_from_string at 512 px long side; lettering uses a hand-built 100-unit block alphabet GLYPHS with only A B C D F H K M N O P R S T U W ! (new words with E/G/I/L/etc. need new glyphs).

Tests pinning VFX art: test_every_word_has_lettering_and_the_set_is_8_to_10_words (test_vfx.gd:251) and test_fx_art_is_512_px_with_svg_sources_and_logged (1061: every PNG max side == 512, an .svg source, an ASSETS.md mention). No test pins any room material, sky, sun, fog or tonemap. HUD pinned by test_ui, test_rear_warning (rect inside the 20% corner, 1920x1080 'shipped canvas'), test_health_bars. Baseline [V]: test_vfx 53/53, test_hit_flash 13, test_ui 34, test_rear_warning 29, test_humanoid_rig 57, test_crowd_room 18, compile tests green, 0 errors.

HUD is entirely code-drawn (HudStyle _draw helpers, Hud CanvasLayer layer 10, process_priority 100, 1920x1080 canvas); only texture is rear_warning.png; text is ThemeDB.fallback_font emboldened 0.9; no font asset or Theme. VFX canvas layers: SpeedLines layer 5, ImpactFrame layer 20 (reads the whole screen incl. HUD and any 3D post). Impact-frame, flash and sprite draw priorities: flash RENDER_PRIORITY_MIN, comic sprites 0..3.

Capture tooling [V]: tools/capture_bot.sh <scene> <outdir> "<act filter>" <stills fps> records with Movie Maker; real size is 1600x900 (project window override beats --resolution 1280x720), about 4x real time; sheets via ffmpeg tile (use -fps_mode vfr, not -vsync). Existing ~1 m acts: punk_bot 'Punk wind-up at 1 m' (training room; ran clean, 228 frames), 'Punk two-hit punch lands' etc. at 0.95-1.0 m, vfx_bot 'damage looks held at 1 m' (dummy), crowd 'Final pound at 0.9/1.1 m' (boss). No Punk idle+motion+attack clip at 1 m.

To add a 1 m act: new tests/bot/acts/look_acts.gd with static acts(bot) (crowd_bot._collect_acts loads *_acts.gd) using bot.god(), bot.freeze_ai(true), bot.spawn(&"punk", Vector2(0,1.0)), force_attack(0), _look_to(+8) for a face shot [V via a scratch subclass run with -s runner + --write-movie, 887 frames, 0 errors]. AI-driven circling at 1 m fails: with posture_ring_min/max = 1.0 the Punk attacks at once then stands in RECOVER for the 5 s cooldown; motion must be scripted via rig.play / play_locomotion / play_move.

Perf act 'Perf, six with ragdolls' (crowd_acts.gd:86, windowed, not recording): M3 recorded p95 12.2-13.1 ms and spawn hitch 25-31.5 ms (limit 33). My re-run today was contaminated (load average 7.45: Blender, Codex renderer, other Godot): mean 16.6-17.5, p95 30-40, worst 56.4, probe R15 p95 20.0 / spawn 38.9 (miss). Not a valid baseline; compare pre-M4 and M4 branches back to back on a quiet machine.

New shaders/materials need a first-use warm-up: the project measured 8-16 ms hitches on first draw of each material variant (VfxDirector.begin_warm_up at vfx_director.gd:170, HumanoidRig._warm_flash at humanoid_rig.gd:501). A new Tuning group (e.g. Look) requires regenerating tuning/default.json (tools/gen_default_preset.gd; test_tuning_panel.gd:454 compares).
verified_by_running: Copied tools/gen_fx.gd to a scratch project and ran it headless: 29 SVG + 29 PNG regenerated in 0.8 s, all cmp-identical to the committed files.

Ran a windowed SceneTree prototype (edge_proto.gd) in the crowd room with two Punks: a full-screen spatial quad using hint_depth_texture + hint_normal_roughness_texture produced ink edge lines in first person and side view with MSAA 4x; saved base/edges/depth/normal stills.
Ran edge_cost.gd (3 runs total): unvsynced wall frame times with and without the quad variants and with MSAA 4x vs off; found viewport_get_measured_render_time_gpu returns 0.00 on this Metal setup.
Verified headless Godot parses shaders (bad .gdshader prints SHADER ERROR at load) and that built-ins like INV_PROJECTION_MATRIX are not accessible inside helper functions.
Ran tools/capture_bot.sh res://tests/bot/punk_bot.tscn ... "Punk wind-up at 1 m" 6: exit 0, 0 errors, 1600x900, 228 frames, 23 stills; tiled a contact sheet with ffmpeg.

Ran a scratch crowd-room bot (extends crowd_bot, started by a -s runner with --write-movie) with three 1 m Punk acts: 887 frames, 0 errors; confirmed AI-driven circling at 1 m fails (attack then RECOVER).
Re-ran the 'Perf, six with ragdolls' act windowed (contaminated by system load average 7.45): mean 16.6-17.5 ms, p95 30-40 ms, R15 miss; documented as not a valid baseline.

Ran GUT headless one file at a time: test_vfx 53/53, test_hit_flash 13/13, test_ui 34/34, test_rear_warning 29/29, test_crowd_room 18/18, test_health_bars 6/6, test_armor_presentation 8/8, test_pickup_cue 7/7, test_humanoid_rig 57/57, test_scripts_compile 2/2, test_bot_scripts_compile 2/2, no SCRIPT/SHADER ERROR.

Dumped the Godot 4.7.2 class reference to the shared scratch godot-doc dir (descriptions are empty but members exist) to confirm Compositor/CompositorEffect, Camera3D/WorldEnvironment.compositor, Environment.adjustment_color_correction and Viewport.screen_space_aa.
open_questions: Outline method for characters: separate inverted-hull meshes (copy render layers, shadow off) vs a next_pass chain (conflicts with the hit-flash next_pass and its tests) vs screen-space only. The rig owner must decide together with the flash and damage-look rewrite.

Edge pass as a world-node quad (worked) vs a CompositorEffect (compute, can run before transparents; not tried). M1 cost of the buffers (+2.3 to +3.6 ms) may need a Tuning toggle or MSAA off + FXAA on the Mac; RTX 3060 cost is unmeasured.
Should test_room.gd (frozen for M3) be changed to call RoomKit so one place holds the sky, materials and post for every bot?

Is it acceptable to change the 512 px VFX PNG rule (pinned by test_vfx.gd:1061, stated in SPEC §10)? Otherwise the final pass is style work (halftone, per-tier variants, ink weight matched to the 3D outline) within 512 px.

Draw order of the edge quad against the hit-flash overlay and comic sprites is untested (proposed render_priority around -127); fog is applied before the quad so distant lines stay full-strength unless faded by depth.
FXAA (Viewport.screen_space_aa), CompositorEffect, Environment.adjustment_color_correction LUT and .gdshaderinc includes exist in the 4.7.2 class dump but were not rendered or tested.
FPView raycasts only primitive meshes; who updates it (and R4/R8 of the readability probe) when the Punk becomes a skinned ArrayMesh?
A clean perf baseline on a quiet machine is still needed (my re-run was load-contaminated); GPU time cannot be read in-engine on this Mac.

summary: Reference for the M4 pipeline scripts covering Tripo v3 and Gemini image generation, with a recommended route from a picked concept to a rigged GLB and a credit budget. The most important finding is that the handoff's Tripo route (api.tripo3d.ai/v2/openapi) is scheduled to shut down on 2026-10-31. Our global key works on the v3 API at https://openapi.tripo3d.ai/v3 (balance 1500.00 confirmed) and is rejected by the China hosts. Pricing is in the file: H3.1 image or multiview to 3D costs 30 credits with standard texture, rig 25, each preset animation 10, rig-check free, and P-series 100-130 per task. The recommended route is Gemini orthographic A-pose views, then multiview-to-model on H3.1 (about 30 credits), rig-check (free), rig on v3.0 with spec "unity" (25), then retarget presets (10 each). A first accepted Punk costs about 105 to 210 credits, and 800 credits fund roughly 13 fully rigged attempts or 23 generations plus the final rig and animations. Tripo does not document its rig's bone names, rest pose or hierarchy. Godot's SkeletonProfileHumanoid (verified by running: 56 bones, Unity HumanBodyBones names, T-pose reference) should match spec "unity", but this is unverified until one real rig is dumped in Blender.
key_facts: Tripo v2 (api.tripo3d.ai/v2/openapi, the route in HANDOFF) shuts down 2026-10-31 per the official SDK page; use v3 at https://openapi.tripo3d.ai/v3 with 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'. Verified: GET /v3/account/balance returns balance 1500.00, frozen 0.00 and /v3/account/usage returns [].

Our key is a global-account key: openapi.tripo3d.com/v3 and api.tripo3d.com/v2 return 401, api.tripo3d.ai/v3 returns 404. Docs host is developers.tripo3d.ai (USD, 1 credit = $0.01); every doc page is fetchable as raw Markdown at /en/docs/<id>.md; copies are in scratchpad/m4-read-tripo-gemini/docs-raw/.

v3 uses one endpoint per task with a unified 'input' field (task_id, file_token, or URL): generation/image-to-model, generation/multiview-to-model, models/texture, models/convert, mesh/decimate, mesh/uv, animations/rig-check, animations/rig, animations/retarget. Polling is GET /v3/tasks/{id}; statuses are queued, running, success, failed, cancelled, banned, expired. Real task ids are UUIDs. Stylize and refine are retired.

Download URLs in task output expire after 5 minutes. Download immediately in the same run and send no Authorization header to the CDN. Batch retarget returns output.model_urls (plural). credits_consumed and balance are floats.

Credit table: H3.1/H3.0/H2.5 image or multiview to 3D 20 untextured, 30 standard texture, 40 detailed, 50 8K, plus 20 for geometry_quality detailed, 5 for quad, 10 for smart_low_poly. P1/P2 cost 100/110/120/130. Texture task 10/10/20/30, convert 5 (10 advanced), retopo v3.0 35, Smart UV 20, rig-check free, auto rig 25, retarget 10 per animation (max 5 per task).

Recommended generation call: multiview-to-model with model v3.1-20260211, front/left/back(/right) as view-key objects with file_tokens, texture true, pbr false, texture_quality standard, texture_version v3.5-20260815 with delight true (cost of v3.5 on generation unstated), orientation align_image, face_limit about 20000, fixed model_seed. Leave export_orientation, quad (forces FBX), compress and generate_parts unset. Re-texture with a new texture_seed costs 10 instead of 30.

Rig: v1.0 (default) is biped only with 90+ presets including box_01-03, front_kick_01-02, hit_to_head/body/side/stomach, hurt, fall, idle, walk, run, turn, but cannot use spec unity, unreal or vrm. v3.0-20260909 is recommended for humanoids, accepts spec tripo, mixamo, actorcore, unity, unreal or vrm, and has only 11 biped presets (idle, walk, run, dive, climb, jump, slash, shoot, hurt, fall, turn). Presets must match the rig version. Retarget input is the rig task_id.

Tripo does not document the rig's bone names, count, hierarchy or rest orientation. Independent reviews report no facial joints, no IK chains, over-smoothed shoulder and chest weights, noisy jaw weights, and v3.0 hand bones. The rig is built in the input mesh's pose, so feed an A-pose or T-pose.

Godot 4.7.2 SkeletonProfileHumanoid, verified by running: 56 bones, root_bone Root, scale_base_bone Hips, Unity HumanBodyBones names including 15 finger bones per hand, LeftEye/RightEye/Jaw, T-pose reference. The project's placeholder rig is a 23-name subset. BoneMap (set_skeleton_bone_name and related) allows scripted .tres generation, so spec unity should give an identity map (inferred).

Gemini model ids verified by GET /v1beta/models: gemini-3-pro-image, gemini-3.1-flash-image, gemini-2.5-flash-image (still listed although a pricing page announced shutdown 2026-10-02), plus gemini-nano-banana-2.1 (the docs' new primary), gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image and preview aliases. All support generateContent.

Gemini request: POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent with header x-goog-api-key. generationConfig has responseModalities [TEXT,IMAGE or IMAGE] and imageConfig {aspectRatio, imageSize}; sizes are 512/1K/2K/4K with uppercase K, and 3 Pro starts at 1K. Reference images go in as inline_data parts (up to 14 total, 20 MB request). The response image is in candidates[].content.parts[].inlineData. Licensing: Tripo terms give paid users all rights in outputs and Tripo retains rights on free accounts (the account's paid status is unknown); no attribution is required and no exclusivity is guaranteed. Google claims no ownership of Gemini output; SynthID is embedded.

summary: The Blender 5.2.2 headless clean-up chain (import, scale/apply, normals, voxel remesh, decimate, UV, palette colours, armature from the project's joint table, ARMATURE_AUTO weights, weight transfer, pose-as-rest, head split, GLB export) all works by script, and a skinned mesh can be bound to the project's real HumanoidRig and driven by its procedural animations. The key finding is that the GLB's own Skin cannot be reused (Blender bone axes versus the project's identity-rest, arms-down, -Z-facing skeleton), and Godot's BoneMap/SkeletonProfileHumanoid retarget importer does not produce the project's skeleton either (T-pose, +Z facing, Y-along-bone axes). Instead, recompute the Skin binds in code from the GLB's bind joint positions and the rig's rest directions, keeping the GLB's bind order; I verified this with the real HumanoidRig at heights 1.8 and 2.3 m, in an A-pose and an arms-down mesh, through walk, guard_break and knockdown animations, rendered with Movie Maker. Toon light(), inverted-hull outlines (next_pass and material_overlay), a depth/normal edge quad, a 3D-LUT in Environment and a compute CompositorEffect all work on skinned meshes under Forward+/Metal; the hull adds about 16-19% frame time at 900k skinned triangles on the M1, the edge quad about 3 ms at 720p. Gotchas found: unweighted vertices create a neutral_bone, runtime GLTFDocument skins are unnamed, flat-shaded meshes crack the hull (fix: smooth normals in COLOR), QuadriFlow needs dissolve_degenerate first and still fails for some targets, and exporter bind poses are inconsistent unless the pose is applied as rest. Ragdoll with a skinned body, FP-hidden layers and the existing hit-flash on a toon ShaderMaterial remain unverified.
key_facts: Godot's retarget importer (BoneMap + SkeletonProfileHumanoid, 56 bones) conforms bones to a T-pose, +Z facing, Left at +X, Y-along-bone convention (49 of 56 bones have non-identity global orientation); the project rig is identity rests, arms down, -Z facing, Left at -X (placeholder_body.gd:8-16,45-69), so the importer cannot produce it. Do not use it for the Punk.

Recommended path: export only mesh + weights from Blender (export_animations=False), then in Godot attach the MeshInstance3D under rig.skeleton (skeleton=NodePath('..'), transform identity) with a recomputed Skin: bind' = Scale(rig_scale) * inverse(Transform3D(Basis(R), p)), p = joint position from the GLB's inverse bind, R = shortest-arc rotation from the rig's rest direction (bone to first child) to the GLB's direction; leaf bones take the parent's R; keep the GLB's bind order. Working GDScript is in the doc (section 6.2) and in scratchpad real_rig.gd.

Verified on the real HumanoidRig (MODIFIER_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_MANUAL + skeleton.advance) with walk_forward, guard_break, knockdown_back; rig heights 1.8 and 2.3 m scale correctly; an A-pose (40 deg) mesh and an arms-down mesh both deform right. Naive use of the GLB's own Skin on the project skeleton shreds the mesh.

The Punk needs no animation clips in the GLB: the procedural PlaceholderAnims/PlaceholderPoses drive the skinned mesh. Tripo/Mixamo are only needed for weights/joint positions, and Blender ARMATURE_AUTO on an armature built from the project's joint table does that headless (0.08 s on 5k tris, ~2 s on 85k).

Author the character facing +Y in Blender: the glTF exporter (export_yup=True) maps it to -Z in Godot, the rig's forward (checked via imported AABB). Joint table world positions come from summing BONE_REST (Hips y 0.975, UpperArm x +-0.22 y 1.425, Hand y 0.865, UpperLeg x +-0.11 y 0.925, Foot 0.085, Toes z -0.13); extraction script in scratchpad extract_joints.py.

ARMATURE_AUTO weights leave interior/overlapping vertices unweighted (0 to 240 per test mesh); any unweighted vertex makes Godot's importer add a 'neutral_bone' (24 binds/bones instead of 23). Fix by copying weights from the nearest weighted vertex (KDTree), then vertex_group_limit_total(4) + vertex_group_normalize_all (also silences 'mesh not valid' from weights summing to 1.0000002). Renaming a bone in Blender renames the matching vertex groups.

Runtime GLTFDocument skins have unnamed binds (get_bind_name '' and get_bind_bone = skeleton index) even with GLTFState.use_named_skin_binds=true; the editor import path (skins/use_named_skins=true default) gives named binds. Resolve names through the source skeleton at runtime.

Exporter bind poses: with the armature posed and export_rest_position_armature=True (default) the pose is ignored (A-pose exported); with False the skeleton is exported posed but the Skin binds stay at the A-pose (inconsistent); only 'apply pose as rest' (modifier_apply Armature on the mesh, then pose.armature_apply(selected=False), re-add the modifier) gives consistent arms-down rest and binds. All three work headless.

Remesh/decimate: Decimate COLLAPSE 85k->15k tris in 0.5 s and keeps vertex groups; voxel remesh 12 mm in 0.12 s gives a closed single-shell mesh but drops UVs and vertex groups; QuadriFlow works headless on clean meshes but refused the voxel body until dissolve_degenerate(0.0002)+delete_loose+normals_make_consistent, then still failed for some targets ('wrong init'); property is smooth_normals. Order: voxel remesh -> decimate -> UV -> weights.

Palette colours without Cycles: smart_project + pack_islands (0.6 s on 15k tris), k-means or fixed palette, per-face palette-cell UVs on a 64x8 atlas with Closest sampler (Godot imports it as texture_filter=2) or a CORNER colour attribute exported with export_vertex_color='ACTIVE' (Godot ARRAY_COLOR, vertex_color_use_as_albedo stays false). For a retopologised mesh, BVHTree.find_nearest into the original textured mesh + barycentric UV gave 92.1% correct palette index on a 3k-tri mesh in 0.06 s.

Head split: select faces by mean Head weight > 0.5 and bpy.ops.mesh.separate(type='SELECTED'); the new object keeps all vertex groups, the Armature modifier and parent; Godot imports the parts as separate MeshInstance3Ds sharing one Skin, so each can have its own visual layer (FP-hidden), material and shadow setting.

Toon shader on skinned meshes works: light() with ATTENUATION (includes the shadow), 2-threshold smoothstep bands with tinted shadow, hard step specular, stepped rim. Inverted hull (render_mode unshaded, cull_front, VERTEX += NORMAL * width * clamp(dist/ref, min, max)) follows skinned poses and works both as next_pass and as material_overlay (recommend material_overlay, keeping next_pass free for the rig's hit-flash overlay). Hard-edged meshes crack the hull; smooth normals stored in vertex COLOR fix it (verified on a cube).

Screen-space edge pass: QuadMesh 2x2 child of the Camera3D, extra_cull_margin 16384, render_mode unshaded, depth_test_disabled, skip_vertex_transform, POSITION = vec4(VERTEX.xy,1,1), hint_screen_texture + hint_depth_texture + hint_normal_roughness_texture all work in Forward+/Metal (view-space normals include skinning); no ALPHA needed. Environment.adjustment_color_correction accepts an ImageTexture3D LUT (works); a compute CompositorEffect loading an imported .glsl RDShaderFile works on Metal (avoid runtime shader_compile_spirv_from_source).

Cost on M1/Metal 1280x720, 60 skinned 15k-tri characters (900k tris), uncapped wall ms/frame: StandardMaterial3D 6.20, toon 6.03, toon+hull overlay 7.02, toon+hull next_pass 7.19, +hull+edge quad 10.14. GPU timestamps read 0 on Metal, so only relative numbers; Movie Maker ignores --resolution and records the project window size.

Process traps: `-s` SceneTree scripts cannot see autoloads at compile time (run a scene instead: godot --path <repo> <abs .tscn>); a script error before quit() hangs the process; zsh does not word-split unquoted $args; the doctool dump has signatures only. Skinned-mesh culling follows the skeleton pose (no custom_aabb needed for a 1.6 m hips move).
